newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday February 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday February 24.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* After a three-day national congress, Massimo D'Alema was re-elected leader of the Democratic Party of the Left, but the hard-left side of the party along with trade unions criticised his position on welfare reforms (all).

* In an interview, hard-left Communist Refoundation Party President Armando Cossutta blamed PDS for "turning to the right" and said now Prime Minister Romano Prodi stands in a much weaker position (Corriere della Sera).
* A report from economic research institute Isco said in 1997 the fiscal burden will reach 43.5 percent of GDP, a record level due to the introduction of the Eurotax (all).
* Prodi and Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi are expected to meet majority parties leaders to outline the deficit-cutting measures to be included in an additional minibudget (all).
* The board of Istituto San Paolo di Torino is expected to meet today to examine 1996 results and present plans to privatise the bank (La Repubblica).
* The shareholders assembly of state telecom holding Stet should name tomorrow the new board which will lead the merger with Telecom Italia (La Repubblica).
* In a poll, 67 percent of respondents said they were quite favourable or rather favourable to the single European currency (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
